decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom required heavy development investment and supports the firm's high-end QA positioning, so management would attribute its reduced web visibility in 2019 to the slow, project-based particle therapy market rather than failure.

Small volume chambers are core dosimetry consumables tied to the firm's decades of calibration expertise and remained prominently presented, so dropping them would contradict its announced integrated QA direction.
This chamber is part of the firm's committed detector portfolio, kept a dedicated page through 2019, and fits the connected QA platform, so management persists with it.
The multi-model standard clinical chamber line is central to the reference dosimetry business with accredited calibration, making it a highly committed, long-lived product.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and scanning systems, so its investment and strategic fit favor keeping it.
Thimble chambers are staple dosimetry products with long clinical lifecycles and stable presentation, and nothing suggests the firm would abandon this committed line.
